According to ArtHouse Jersey, the initiative for quarterly funding provides financial support and assistance for the development of new projects, as well as aiding applicants looking to build a career in the arts.
A public artwork is also planned for the area.
The ceramic art project, alongside other upgrades to the area, were funded by the UK Shared Prosperity Fund in collaboration with Ards and North Down Borough Council, costing £130,000 in total.
Applications for the grants run until 25 July, and are themed around young people and families, identity and sense of place, community and creativity, research and resources and lifelong learning.
